questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Given that $a\cdot b=-8$, find the angle between $a=⟨2t,2t⟩$ and $b=⟨4,-2⟩.$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $a\cdot b=-8$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-8 \\ 2t\cdot 4+2t\cdot (-2) & =-8 \\ 8t-4t & =-8 \\ 4t & =-8 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨2(-2),\,2(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-8}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{8}{4\sqrt{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{5}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}})≈{108.4}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}x=⟨-1,0,3⟩,\,y=⟨-2,2,3⟩,\,z=⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△XYZ$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠XZY=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038738/assets/87453fecb9da6b9e673ab5a85a289a3fac73f4fb90fc8f1b33e7c0a80b1ea77f.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ZX} & =x-z \\  & =⟨-1,0,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{ZY} & =y-z \\  & =⟨-2,2,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{ZX}\cdot \overset{\to }{ZY}}{|\overset{\to }{ZX}||\overset{\to }{ZY}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0+1\cdot 3+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={45}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨3,3,-5⟩,\,q=⟨4,2,-3⟩,\,r=⟨7,5,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038738/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨4,2,-3⟩-⟨3,3,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨7,5,-3⟩-⟨3,3,-5⟩ \\  & =⟨4,2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 4+(-1)\cdot 2+2\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{24}} \\  & =\frac{6}{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨-5,1,3⟩,\,q=⟨-3,-1,2⟩,\,r=⟨-5,2,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038738/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨-3,-1,2⟩-⟨-5,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨-5,2,4⟩-⟨-5,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={135}^{∘}.
$$

questions.problem: Given that $a\cdot b=-9$, find the angle between $a=⟨-2t,3t⟩$ and $b=⟨3,1⟩.$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $a\cdot b=-9$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-9 \\ -2t\cdot 3+3t\cdot 1 & =-9 \\ -6t+3t & =-9 \\ -3t & =-9 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨-2(3),\,3(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,9⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-9}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{9}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{\sqrt{117}\cdot \sqrt{10}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{3\sqrt{13}\cdot \sqrt{10}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{130}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{3}{\sqrt{130}})≈{105.3}^{∘}.
$$
